--- title: "[GAMLSSFamily]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-abc}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Abstract base class for GAMLSS distributional families. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L14-L279){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python GAMLSSFamily() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Ordinary `Family` subclasses (used by `GAM`) model only the mean `mu` of the response as a function of covariates, treating any other distributional parameters (e.g. the variance or dispersion) as constant across observations. A `GAMLSSFamily`, used by `GAMLSS` instead of `GAM`, generalizes the single-parameter `Family` abstraction to the location-scale-shape setting: instead of one response parameter with a mean link, it defines a full response distribution with `K` named parameters $\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_K$ (e.g. location `mu` and scale `sigma`), each with its own link function $g_k$ and its own additive predictor $\eta_k = g_k(\theta_k)$. This is useful whenever more than the mean of the response changes systematically with covariates — for example, when the spread (heteroscedasticity), skew, or zero-inflation probability also varies across the range of the predictors. `GAMLSS` fits every parameter's additive predictor jointly by alternating penalized IRLS updates across parameters (the RS algorithm), which relies on each family supplying the per-parameter score `dl_dtheta`, (expected) Fisher information `d2l_dtheta2`, link/inverse-link/link-derivative, log-likelihood, initial values, and a `simulate` method. Subclasses must implement all of the abstract methods below. Whittaker ships with the following concrete GAMLSS families: - `GaussianLS` — location-scale Gaussian: identity link for the mean, log link for the standard deviation. - `GammaLS` — location-scale Gamma: log link for both the mean and the coefficient of variation. - `BetaLS` — mean-precision Beta: logit link for the mean, log link for the precision. - `ZeroInflatedPoisson` — Poisson mean plus a zero-inflation probability, for count data with excess zeros. - `ZeroInflatedNegativeBinomial` — overdispersed counts with excess zeros, combining `NegativeBinomial`-style overdispersion with zero-inflation. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} GAMLSS families are passed to `GAMLSS`, and each distributional parameter gets its own formula: ::: {#dbd26611 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.sin(x) sigma = 0.2 + 0.3 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) y = rng.normal(mu, sigma) data = {"x": x, "y": y} # Model both the mean and the standard deviation as smooth functions of x model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "sigma": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.GaussianLS(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: GaussianLS(mu=identity, sigma=log) N obs: 300 Global deviance: 271.2831 AIC: 297.3004 BIC: 345.4816 Log-likelihood: -135.6416 Converged: True (4 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 6.63 Smooth 1: edf = 5.63 --- sigma --- EDF total: 6.38 Smooth 1: edf = 5.38 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
parameter_names Names of the distributional parameters modeled by this family.
### [parameter_names]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Names of the distributional parameters modeled by this family. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [parameter_names]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[str, ...]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every concrete `GAMLSSFamily` names its parameters explicitly, e.g. `('mu', 'sigma')` for `GaussianLS` and `GammaLS`, or `('mu', 'phi')` for `BetaLS`. `GAMLSS` uses this tuple to determine which formulas it expects (one per name) and the order in which it cycles through parameters during the RS fitting algorithm. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
d2l_dtheta2() Negative expected second derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`.
dl_dtheta() First derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`.
initialize() Starting values for all distributional parameters given `y`.
link() Apply the link function for `param`: `eta = g(theta)`.
link_derivative() Derivative of the link for `param`: `d(eta)/d(theta)`.
link_inverse() Apply the inverse link for `param`: `theta = g^-1(eta)`.
log_likelihood() Full log-likelihood evaluated at the given parameter values.
simulate() Simulate response values from the distribution.
### [d2l_dtheta2()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Negative expected second derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L185-L211){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python d2l_dtheta2(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the (expected) Fisher information $-E[\partial^2 \ell / \partial \theta^2]$ for `param`, evaluated elementwise at the current parameter estimates. Must return positive values, since it is used directly as a working weight during fitting: it both scales the working pseudo-response and forms the diagonal weight matrix for the penalized IRLS update of `param`'s additive predictor. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the distributional parameter to differentiate with respect to, one of `parameter_names`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates of all distributional parameters, keyed by name, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise working weights, shape `(n,)`, guaranteed positive. ::: ### [dl_dtheta()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} First derivative of the log-likelihood with respect to `param`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L158-L183){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python dl_dtheta(param, y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns $\partial \ell / \partial \theta$ evaluated elementwise at the current parameter estimates. This score forms the basis of the working pseudo-response used by `GAMLSS`'s RS algorithm when updating the additive predictor for `param`, holding the other distributional parameters fixed. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the distributional parameter to differentiate with respect to, one of `parameter_names`. [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates of all distributional parameters, keyed by name, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise first derivatives, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for all distributional parameters given `y`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L237-L255){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Produces a reasonable initial guess for every parameter in `parameter_names` from the raw response alone, before any covariate information is used. `GAMLSS` uses these as the starting point for the first RS iteration. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Initial values for each parameter, keyed by name, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the link function for `param`: `eta = g(theta)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L91-L111){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Maps a distributional parameter from its natural scale (e.g. `mu` on the real line, `sigma > 0`) onto the unconstrained scale of the additive predictor `eta`, so that `GAMLSS` can model it with an ordinary smooth linear predictor. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the distributional parameter being linked, one of `parameter_names`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linked values `eta = g(theta)`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the link for `param`: `d(eta)/d(theta)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L135-L156){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_derivative(param, values) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Used by the RS algorithm to convert the score `dl_dtheta` into a working pseudo-response on the scale of the additive predictor, via the chain rule $\partial \ell / \partial \eta = (\partial \ell / \partial \theta)\, (d\eta/d\theta)^{-1}$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the distributional parameter being linked, one of `parameter_names`. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale at which to evaluate the derivative, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Elementwise derivatives `d(eta)/d(theta)`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse link for `param`: `theta = g^-1(eta)`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L113-L133){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python link_inverse(param, eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Maps the additive predictor back onto the natural scale of the parameter, enforcing any constraints (e.g. positivity for a scale parameter, or the unit interval for a probability) implied by the chosen link. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [param]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the distributional parameter being linked, one of `parameter_names`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Additive predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Parameter values on the natural scale, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Full log-likelihood evaluated at the given parameter values. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L213-L235){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python log_likelihood(y, params) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Sums the per-observation log-density of the response distribution across all observations, using the current estimate of every distributional parameter. Used for convergence checks during fitting and for computing information criteria such as AIC/BIC in model summaries. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values, shape `(n,)`. [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current estimates of all distributional parameters, keyed by name, each of shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood summed over all observations. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate response values from the distribution. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/docs-user-guide-improvements/whittaker/families/gamlss_base.py#L257-L279){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python simulate(params, rng) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Draws one random sample per observation from the response distribution at the given per-observation parameter values. Used for posterior/parametric-bootstrap style simulation from a fitted `GAMLSS` model. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Distributional parameter values to simulate from, keyed by name, each of shape `(n,)`. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A NumPy random generator (e.g. `numpy.random.default_rng()`) used to draw the simulated values. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, shape `(n,)`. :::
